'''Ronald Lancaster''' {{postnominals|country=GBR|size=100%|MBE|CChem|FRSC}} (9 March 1931 – 18 October 2026) was an English [[Church of England|Anglican]] clergyman, chemist, businessman and teacher, having taught chemistry at [[Kimbolton School]] from 1963 to 1988. He was a [[fireworks]] manufacturer, having founded and remained owner of [[Kimbolton Fireworks]], the last manufacturer of fireworks in the UK before their closure in February 2019.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/uk-england-cambridgeshire-47289747|title = Kimbolton Fireworks ceases trading after 55 years|work = BBC News|date = 19 February 2019}}</ref><ref name="175faces">{{cite web |title=Reverend Ronald Lancaster MBE CChem FRSC |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20190705044735/http://www.rsc.org:80/diversity/175-faces/all-faces/reverend-ronald-lancaster-mbe-cchem-frsc/|archivedate=5 July 2019|url=http://www.rsc.org/diversity/175-faces/all-faces/reverend-ronald-lancaster-mbe-cchem-frsc |website=175 Faces of Chemistry |publisher=[[Royal Society of Chemistry]]}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/av/business-24809743 |title="Master Pastor Blaster" at UK's last fireworks factory |work=BBC News|date=5 November 2013 |access-date=25 November 2017}}</ref>

==Life and career==
Lancaster was born on 9 March 1931, in [[Huddersfield]], West Yorkshire, where he also grew up.<ref name="teleobit">{{cite news |title=The Rev Ronald Lancaster, school chaplain and ‘Master Blaster Pastor’ who founded Kimbolton Fireworks |url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/obituaries/2026/10/19/kimbolton-fireworks-chaplain-ronald-lancaster-chemistry/ |access-date=19 October 2026 |publisher=The Telegraph |date=19 October 2026}}</ref> It was here that [[Standard Fireworks]] and [[Lion Fireworks]] were based.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.dur.ac.uk/resources/ceremonies/congregation/lancaster_ronald.pdf |title=Ronald Lancaster, Master of Science, Durham Cathedral, 1 July 2009 |first=Martyn |last=Chamberlain |authorlink=Martyn Chamberlain |publisher=Durham University |accessdate=25 November 2017}}</ref><ref>{{cite news |url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/news/celebritynews/my-perfect-weekend/8866624/My-perfect-weekend-Rev-Ron-Lancaster.html |title=My perfect weekend: Rev. Ron Lancaster |newspaper=[[The Daily Telegraph]] |date=3 November 2011 |accessdate=25 November 2017}}</ref> He became interested in fireworks after the [[Coronation of King George VI and Queen Elizabeth|coronation of George VI]] in 1937. He attended [[King James's School, Almondbury|King James's School]] in [[Almondbury]] from 1942 to 1950,<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.oas.org.uk/Ron%20Lancaster%20audio%20page.php |title=Rev Ron Lancaster MBE (1942–50) |website=Old Almondbury Society |date=3 October 2006 |accessdate=25 November 2017}}</ref> and then studied psychology at [[St John's College, Durham|St John's College]], [[Durham University]] from 1950.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|title=Lancaster, Rev. Ronald, (born 9 March 1931), Founder, 1964, Managing Director, 1986–2006, Director and Chairman, 2007–19, Kimbolton Fireworks Limited|url=https://www.ukwhoswho.com/view/10.1093/ww/9780199540884.001.0001/ww-9780199540884-e-42824|access-date=2021-05-20|website=WHO'S WHO & WHO WAS WHO|language=en|doi=10.1093/ww/9780199540884.013.u42824|isbn=978-0-19-954088-4}}</ref>

After national service, he studied theology at [[Cuddesdon]] in Oxfordshire between 1955 and 1957.<ref name="Crockford" /> He was [[ordained]] in the [[Church of England]] as a [[Deacon#Anglicanism|deacon]] in 1957 and as a [[Priest#Anglican or Episcopalian|priest]] in 1958.<ref name="Crockford">{{Crockford| surname = Lancaster | forenames = Ronald | id = 39695 | accessed = 3 October 2023}}</ref> He served his [[curacy]] at St Peter's Church, [[Morley, West Yorkshire]] in the [[Diocese of Wakefield]].<ref name=":0" /> He then moved to [[St Peter's Church, Harrogate]] in the [[Diocese of Ripon]], serving as an assistant curate from 1960 to 1963.<ref name="Crockford" />

He took up the post of chaplain and chemistry teacher at [[Kimbolton School]] in 1963. Later that year, he began producing fireworks at a workshop on the school grounds; the following year, with several other members of staff, he set up [[Kimbolton Fireworks]] to make pyrotechnics for public displays.<ref>{{cite web |title=Kimbolton Fireworks: Rev Ron Lancaster honoured with plaque |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/uk-england-cambridgeshire-21847802 |date=20 March 2013 |work=BBC News|accessdate=10 June 2015}}</ref> The public displays put on by Kimbolton Fireworks include the [[Silver Jubilee of Elizabeth II|25th anniversary of the Queen's coronation]] in 1978, the 50th anniversary of [[VJ Day]] in 1995, the [[Transfer of sovereignty over Hong Kong|Hong Kong handover]] in 1997, and at the opening and closing ceremonies of the [[2012 Summer Olympics]] in London.

With [[Takeo Shimizu]], he published ''Fireworks: Principles and Practice'' in 1972; the fourth edition, described as the "bible of fireworks", was published in 2005.

Lancaster retired from teaching in 1988. He was given a plaque at the [[Pyrotechnics Guild International]] conference in 1984, dedicated to the "Master Blaster Pastor".{{citation needed|date=April 2020}} He became a [[Member of the Order of the British Empire]] (MBE) in the [[1993 New Year Honours]], for his services to the fireworks industry,<ref name="175faces"/><ref>{{London Gazette |issue=53153 |date=30 December 1992 |page=15 |supp=y}}</ref> and he was presented with a plaque by the [[Royal Society of Chemistry]] in 2013.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.cambridge-news.co.uk/Master-blaster-pastor-Olympic-Queens-Jubilee-fireworks-displaysgobsmacked-blue-plaque-award/story-22362327-detail/story.html |title='Master blaster pastor' behind Olympic and Queen's Jubilee fireworks displays 'gobsmacked' by blue plaque award |newspaper=[[Cambridge Evening News]] |date=20 March 2013 |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20150923224502/http://www.cambridge-news.co.uk/Master-blaster-pastor-Olympic-Queens-Jubilee-fireworks-displaysgobsmacked-blue-plaque-award/story-22362327-detail/story.html |archivedate=23 September 2015 |accessdate=25 November 2017}}</ref>

He was the father of [[Mark Lancaster, Baron Lancaster of Kimbolton|Mark Lancaster]], who served as an explosives expert in the [[Royal Engineers]], and was involved in running the fireworks business before he was elected as [[Conservative Party (UK)|Conservative]] MP for [[Milton Keynes North East (UK Parliament constituency)|Milton Keynes North East]] in 2005. Mark, husband of fellow Conservative MP [[Caroline Dinenage]], stepped down in 2019 and was elevated to the House of Lords in 2020.

Ronald Lancaster died on 18 October 2026, aged 95.<ref name="teleobit"/>
